newsitem.title: USA: USAir to cut costs with streamlined fleet.
newsitem.headline: USAir to cut costs with streamlined fleet.

text.p: USAir Group Inc's order for up to 400 Airbus Industrie aircraft will help the carrier trim operating expenses to better compete with low-cost rivals such as Southwest Airlines Co, analysts said.
USAir agreed to buy 120 Airbus single-aisle A319, A320 and A321 aircraft, with a total list price of about $4.8 billion to $6.6 billion. USAir also has options for up to 280 more aircraft.
The deal will help USAir reduce the types of aircraft in its fleet, which would cut costs for training, maintenance and scheduling.
USAir declined to comment on the possible cost savings it expects from the streamlined fleet.
USAir's unit costs have risen almost 17 percent since 1990 and remain among the highest in the industry.
Last year, the carrier's unit costs were 3.20 cents higher than the industry average of 8.45 cents and about 4.5 cents higher than rival Southwest, according to a Salomon Brothers research report.
USAir must pare back costs to meet increased competition from Southwest and Delta Air Line's Delta Express unit, analysts said.

"USAir takes this important and significant step today in its effort to become the airline of choice and an airline with a competitive cost structure," Stephen Wolf, chairman and chief executive officer said.
USAir declined to comment on the aircraft delivery schedule and which planes it will retire from its fleet of about 390 aircraft.
Analysts expect delivery to begin in 1998 and average about 30 to 40 planes a year.
USAir selected Airbus over rival Boeing Co because Airbus was better able to meet USAir's delivery schedule needs, analysts said.
"Our production flexibility enables us to provide the aircraft on a schedule more suitable for the airline," said Jean Pierson, Airbus's chief executive officer said in a written statement.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
Analysts also expect USAir to order wide-body aircraft as it expands its international operations.
